01.actor: Rav and Rabba bar bar Hana
01.event: Rabba bar bar Hana gave Rav money to buy a piece of land for him, and Rav bought it for himself.
01.turn: The land lay in a valley of violent men who respected Rav but not Rabba bar bar Hana, so only Rav could buy it.
01.outcome: Rav bought it without telling him first, fearing someone else would buy it in the meantime.
01.summary: Rabba bar bar Hana gave Rav money to buy a certain plot of land for him, but Rav bought it for himself. The land was in a valley of violent men who would deal respectfully with Rav but not with Rabba bar bar Hana. Rav did not stop to tell him first, worried that someone else would snap it up in the meantime.

02.actor: Yehuda bar Mareimar, Rav Pappa, and Abba of Sura
02.event: Rav Pappa pressed Yehuda bar Mareimar to come into the house of Abba of Sura while his son's marriage contract was being written.
02.turn: Yehuda's silent presence made Abba of Sura think he was angry, so Abba signed away everything he owned as dowry.
02.outcome: Abba offered to retract, but Yehuda told him not to become a man who goes back on his word.
02.summary: Rav Pappa went to have his son's marriage contract written at the house of Abba of Sura, and Yehuda bar Mareimar came out to escort him but would not go in, fearing his presence would pressure the bride's father into a larger dowry. Rav Pappa forced him to enter; Yehuda sat in silence, and Abba of Sura, thinking he was angry, wrote all his property into the dowry and begged him to speak. Yehuda said he had never wanted this; when Abba offered to retract, Yehuda told him not to make himself a man who goes back on his word.

03.event: A superintendent refused to rent his domain to his neighbors for an eiruv, so they sought a ruling on renting it from his wife.
03.turn: Rav Yehuda bar Oshaya and Rav Mattana had no answer.
03.outcome: Rav Yehuda told them, citing Shmuel, that a man's wife may establish an eiruv without his knowledge.
03.summary: A superintendent living near Rav Yehuda bar Oshaya would not rent his domain to his neighbors so they could carry on Shabbat. They asked Rav Yehuda bar Oshaya, then Rav Mattana, whether they could rent it from his wife, and neither knew. Finally Rav Yehuda told them in Shmuel's name that a man's wife may establish an eiruv without his knowledge.

04.event: Minyamin, a first-generation Egyptian convert, married another first-generation Egyptian convert.
04.outcome: He planned to marry his son to a second-generation Egyptian convert so his grandson could enter the congregation.
04.summary: Rabbi Yehuda recalled his friend Minyamin, an Egyptian convert among Rabbi Akiva's students. Minyamin said he had married a fellow first-generation Egyptian convert and intended to marry his son to a second-generation one, so that his grandson would be permitted to marry into the community.
04.missing: Whether the planned marriage happened; the passage is mostly a reported statement of intent.

05.actor: Rabbi Abba bar Shumni and Rav Menashya bar Yirmeya
05.event: Two sages parting at the ford of the Yofti River agreed each would tell the other a teaching he had not heard.
05.outcome: One defined the difference between someone who has drunk and someone who is drunk; the other taught what one who seizes a convert's property should do to keep it.
05.summary: Rabbi Abba bar Shumni and Rav Menashya bar Yirmeya were taking leave of each other at a river crossing, and agreed each would share a teaching the other had not heard, since parting over a point of law keeps a friend in mind. One explained that a man who has drunk can still speak before a king, while a drunk man cannot. The other taught that whoever takes possession of a dead convert's property should buy a Torah scroll with it so the rest stays with him.
05.missing: The narrative frame has little turn; the actual parting is implied, not shown.

06.event: Levi publicly taught Rabbi's ruling that a bill of divorce written on forbidden items is valid, citing Rabbi by name.
06.turn: The audience did not praise him.
06.outcome: When he taught it in the name of the majority, they praised him.
06.summary: Levi went out and taught Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's ruling that a bill of divorce written on items forbidden for benefit is valid, giving it in Rabbi's name, and his listeners did not praise him. When he taught it as the view of the many, they praised him, showing that the law follows that ruling.

07.missing: Only a question to an elder about when a woman was permitted to remarry; the incident itself and any answer are not given.

08.actor: Rav Pappa and Pappa the ox herder
08.event: Rav Pappa instructed that the name of Pappa the ox herder, who could not sign, be written in saliva for him to trace in ink.
08.summary: Pappa the ox herder could not sign his name as a witness. Rav Pappa ruled that his name should be written for him in saliva so he could trace over it in ink.
08.missing: Little more than a reported ruling; no turn or outcome is told.

09.event: Rabbi Yohanan's students gathered huge quantities of Genosar fruit for him, and he ate it all.
09.turn: After eating so much he swore he had not tasted anything nourishing.
09.outcome: The Gemara corrects his words to 'sustaining food', since fruit does nourish.
09.summary: Rabba bar bar Hana recalled following Rabbi Yohanan to eat the sweet fruit of Genosar, gathering so much that every hundred fruits would overflow a three-se'a basket. Rabbi Yohanan ate them all and then swore he had still not tasted anything nourishing. The Gemara amends his words to say he had not eaten real sustaining food.

10.event: Ravina examined a slaughterer's knife in Babylonia during the lifetime of his teacher Rav Ashi, who challenged him.
10.turn: Ravina cited Rav Hamnuna's precedent; Rav Ashi denied it; Ravina reconciled both versions.
10.outcome: Ravina argued that as Rav Ashi's disciple-colleague he too was permitted to rule.
10.summary: Ravina checked a slaughterer's knife in Babylonia while his teacher Rav Ashi was alive, and Rav Ashi asked why he had done so. Ravina pointed to Rav Hamnuna, who had ruled in Harta De'argez in Rav Hisda's lifetime; Rav Ashi replied the tradition was that Rav Hamnuna had not ruled. Ravina answered that both traditions were true: Rav Hamnuna had not ruled under his main teacher Rav Huna, but did rule under Rav Hisda, whose disciple-colleague he was, and Ravina claimed the same standing with Rav Ashi.
10.missing: Rav Ashi's response to Ravina's final argument.

11.event: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi ruled (or meant to rule) in a case according to the Rabbis of the mishna.
11.turn: Perata objected that this would leave the court no more power than an ordinary person.
11.outcome: Rabbi reversed his ruling (in Rav Safra's version, did not act on it).
11.summary: Rav Dimi reported that in a certain case Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi ruled according to the Rabbis of the mishna. Perata, grandson of Rabbi Perata the Great, objected that the court would then have no advantage over an ordinary person, and Rabbi reversed his decision. In Rav Safra's version, Rabbi only intended to rule that way and, after Perata's objection, did not.

12.missing: Describes Rav Huna's habitual practice with litigants, not a single event.

13.missing: A request, a habit and a ruling about orla; no event unfolds.

14.event: People asked Rabbi Elai where Rabbi Abbahu was hiding.
14.outcome: He answered in riddling language that Abbahu had consulted the Nasi and gone south to the sages there.
14.summary: People asked Rabbi Elai to show them where Rabbi Abbahu was hiding. Rabbi Elai answered in a riddle: Abbahu had taken counsel with 'the one who crowns' (the Nasi) and gone south to 'Mephibosheth', meaning the southern sages.
14.missing: Why Rabbi Abbahu was hiding and what happened afterward.

15.actor: Ravina and the daughter of Rav Ashi
15.event: Ravina collected the dowry share for Rav Ashi's daughter from two heirs.
15.turn: From Mar son of Rav Ashi she got intermediate land with no oath, but from the orphan grandson she got inferior land with an oath.
15.summary: Ravina arranged for Rav Ashi's daughter to receive her tenth of the estate. From her brother Mar son of Rav Ashi she took intermediate-quality land without an oath, but from her orphaned nephew she took only inferior land and had to swear an oath.
15.missing: Mainly a legal precedent; no turn or outcome beyond the ruling.

16.event: Rava bar Avuh collected money on two promissory notes in Mehoza naming Havai bar Nanai and Nanai bar Havai.
16.summary: Two promissory notes surfaced in Mehoza naming Havai bar Nanai and Nanai bar Havai, names that were common there. Rava bar Avuh collected the debts on them anyway, without worrying that they might belong to others of the same name.
16.missing: Only a case cited as legal proof; the rest is argument.

17.event: A man gave Shmuel a hand as he stepped off a ferry.
17.turn: Shmuel learned the man had a case to bring before him.
17.outcome: Shmuel declared himself disqualified from judging the man's case.
17.summary: Shmuel was crossing a river by ferry when a man gave him a hand getting out. Shmuel asked what he was doing there, and the man said he had a case for him to judge. Shmuel told him that this small favor disqualified him from hearing the case.

18.event: Rav Beivai told the sages not to listen to Rav Yosef's attribution of a ruling to Rabbi.
18.turn: Beivai revealed he had taught it to Yosef himself, in the name of Rav Adda bar Ahava, and the word was 'many' (rabbim), not 'Rabbi'.
18.outcome: Rav Yosef exclaimed that he had mistaken 'Rabbi' for 'many'.
18.summary: When Rav Yosef cited a ruling as taught by Rabbi, Rav Beivai told the sages not to listen: he had taught it to Rav Yosef himself, in the name of Rav Adda bar Ahava, and it spoke of 'many' in the outer courtyard. Rav Yosef exclaimed 'Master of Abraham!' and admitted he had confused 'Rabbi' with 'rabbim'.
18.missing: Why Rav Yosef forgot (an illness is mentioned only in the translator's gloss).

19.actor: Rabbi Meir and a man who made an onion eiruv
19.event: A man told Rabbi Meir in Ardiska that he had made his eiruv with onions in order to walk to Tiv'in.
19.turn: Rabbi Meir held the onion eiruv invalid, so the man was outside his Shabbat limit.
19.outcome: Rabbi Meir made him stay within his four cubits.
19.summary: Rabbi Meir was spending Shabbat in Ardiska when a man came and told him he had made his eiruv with onions so he could walk to Tiv'in. Rabbi Meir held that onions do not make a valid eiruv, so the man had already left his Shabbat limit, and he ordered him to stay within his four cubits.

20.event: Rav Hisda's daughter asked her father, who studied through the night, whether he would not sleep a little.
20.outcome: He replied that long days with little chance to study would soon come, and then he would sleep plenty.
20.summary: Rav Hisda spent his nights studying, and his daughter asked if he did not want to sleep a little. He answered that the long days in which no Torah can be studied would come soon enough, meaning death, and then he would sleep a great deal.
